=== George Noelke Objection to Applicants List and Motion to Require Adequate Notice and Hearing.pdf ===
George Noelke, Intervenor, Pro Se, in 59182 and 59475​
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26–16349​
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475


 JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC                             §
 DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA                                   §
 TRANSMISSION SERVICES                                           §       BEFORE THE
 CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR                                      §
 CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND                                 §       STATE OFFICE OF
 NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST                              §
 SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV                            §       ADMINISTRATIVE
 TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL,                              §
 BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,                              §       HEARINGS
 LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD,                                §
 MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM                         §
 GREEN AND WILLIAMSON CRANES COUNTIES                            §



  INTERVENOR GEORGE NOELKE’S OBJECTION TO APPLICANTS’ LIST OF
INTERVENORS WHO DID NOT FILE TESTIMONY OR STATEMENT OF POSITION
   AND MOTION TO PROVIDE NOTICE AND OPPORTUNITY FOR HEARING
             BEFORE INTERVENOR DISMISSAL EN MASSE

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

  I.​   INTRODUCTION
    A.​ George Noelke (“Noelke”), Intervenor in 59182 and 59475 asserts that certain SOAH Orders in
        59475 providing notice to affected landowners that they have been approved as Intervenors are
        procedurally inadequate.
    B.​ Noelke further asserts that Applicants’ “list of Intervenors who did not file testimony or statement
        of position” filed on May 15, 2026, Item 4688, functions as a cloaked Motion to Dismiss and
        thereby violates those Intervenors’ Due Course of Law, Due Process and APA Texas Gov’t Code
        2001.051 rights to fully participate in this contested case.
    C.​ Consequently, the procedural clock in SOAH Order No. 6 should be reset so that an estimated
        895 (eight hundred and ninety five) Intervenors the Applicants seek to dismiss are not
        wrongfully dismissed after failing to receive adequate notice and a hearing regarding the
        procedural requirement that they must file a position statement or direct testimony.
    D.​ Further, Noelke objects to the mechanical en masse dismissal of landowners under 16 TAC §
        22.124 and 22.161. Because Docket Nos. 59475 and 59182 are operationally interdependent



                                                                                                          1
        components of the same 765-kV backbone, the premature termination of party status for hundreds
       of eastern-segment landowners, possibly as many as half of the intervenors, fundamentally
       distorts the routing calculus for the entire integrated project. It deprives remaining Intervenors of
       a complete, accurate, and adversarial record regarding alternative constraints, violating Texas
       Government Code § 2001.051, Due Course of Law and Due Process. An en masse dismissal of
       the magnitude sought by Applicants ought to shock the conscience and raise serious doubts about
       whether this hearings process is meaningful for all Intervenors.
   E.​ Noelke has timely filed this Objection and Motion, as it is filed by him prior to any action taken
       by this Court on the merits of Applicant’s list of Intervenors who did not file Testimony or
       Statement of Position.​


II.​   PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND
   A.​ Noelke was first approved as an Intervenor in CCN 59182 at SOAH Order No. 6, Item 132, with
       the following notice in that Order: “Intervenors are advised that a procedural schedule was
       set in this case in SOAH Order No. 5 on February 11, 2026. As stated in that order, any
       intervenor who does not file testimony or a statement of position by the prescribed deadline
       will be dismissed as a party and prohibited from participating in the hearing on the merits
       and briefing.” Indeed, a review of SOAH Order No. 5 in 59182 shows that the ALJs are relying
       upon 16 TAC 22.124 and 22.161. See page 13 of Item 79.
   B.​ Noelke timely filed his request to intervene in 59475 on April 27. See Item 3199. Noelke was
       acutely aware of the procedural timelines set forth in SOAH Order No. 6, Item 788. That order
       states: “A party who fails to file either direct testimony or a statement of position is subject to
       being dismissed as a party. Accordingly, the ALJs hereby give notice that if an intervenor fails to
       file either written direct testimony or a statement of position by the prescribed deadline of May
       13, 2026, the ALJs will dismiss them as a party unless that intervenor, by May 20,2026, files a
       response setting forth good cause for failing to comply and requests a hearing on that issue.
       Intervenors who are dismissed will be prohibited from participating in the hearing on the merits
       and briefing.”See Item 788.
   C.​ Noelke, seeing the over 1,500 requests to intervene overwhelm the PUC interchange, decided to
       err on the side of caution and file his Statement of Position on May 9 before he had been
       admitted as an Intervenor and before the May 13 deadline as required by SOAH Order No. 6.
       Indeed, May 13 came and went without Noelke receiving notice that he had been admitted as an
       intervenor. Seeing another critical deadline approaching, May 15 to file discovery on Applicants
       per SOAH Order No. 6, Noelke timely filed RFI’s on Applicants on May 15 also before he had


                                                                                                               2
     been admitted as an intervenor. See Item 4651. Noelke fully disclosed to this Court and to the
    Applicants that he was filing his Statement of Position and RFI’s without yet being ruled an
    Intervenor by the Court.
D.​ On May 15, 2026 at 2:34 pm this Court filed its SOAH Order No. 14, and that order listed
    Noelke (at page 33) and literally hundreds of other landowners as accepted as intervenors in
    59475. See Item 4679. Noticeably absent from this Order is any reference to SOAH Order No. 6’s
    requirement that Intervenors must file either a Statement of Position or Direct Testimony by May
    13, 2026. Indeed it would be impossible to impose such an explicit deadline because that May 13,
    2026 deadline had lapsed by the time Order No. 14 had been filed on the Interchange on May 15,
    2026.
E.​ May 15, 2026 was also the deadline for Applicants to file their list of Intervenors who did not file
    a Statement of Position or Direct Testimony. See SOAH Order No. 6, Item 788 at page 5. They
    filed ONCOR AND LCRA TSC'S LIST OF INTERVENORS WHO DID NOT FILE
    TESTIMONY OR A STATEMENT OF POSITION at 4:33 pm on May 15, 2026 only 1 hour and
    59 minutes after SOAH filed its SOAH Order No. 14. See Item 4688 Two things are noticeably
    absent from their filing. First, Noelke’s name is not listed, so presumably his filing his Statement
    of Position before he was determined to be a party successfully kept him out of this procedural
    trap. And, second, no where in the document are the Applicants moving for sanctions under 16
    TAC 22.124 and 22.161 That is, the Applicants are not asking the Court to sanction landowners
    who fail to comply with limiting or disallowing the offending party's rights to participate in the
    proceeding as set forth in 16 TAC.161 (b)(8). They merely state, in effect, that they are complying
    with SOAH Order No. 6 to list the failing Intervenors.
F.​ The ALJ’s in 59475 have issued multiple orders admitting landowners as Intervenors.
    Presumably, Intervenors in SOAH Orders No. 2, 3 and 5 received fair notice of their obligation to
    file a Position Statement or Direct Testimony because they received notice of that requirement by
    service of SOAH Order 6. But, see Orders 9 (Item 2904 ), 10 (Item 3681) and 14 (Item 4679).
    These orders entirely fail to refer to the SOAH Order No. 6 requirement to file a Statement of
    Position or Direct Testimony. These intervenors, thereby, have no actual notice of Applicants’
    “list”, which is for all practical purposes a statement of their default.
G.​ Noelke’s observation that Applicants’ list of Intervenors who did not file a Statement of Position
    or Direct Testimony is used for en masse dismissal of Intervenors is not theoretical. See for
    example, SOAH Order No. 10 in 59182, Item 255. Noelke asserts that not all Intervenors in
    59182 received the notice of Order 6 that he did, yet, Order 10 in fact dismissed certain
    Intervenors for failing to file a Statement of Position or Direct Testimony according to the list


                                                                                                         3
       provided by Applicants. See also Applicants’ list at Item242. Even in another related CCN,
      59029, the Applicants and this Court used the same procedural tools to dismiss Intervenors. See
      Item 267 in 59029. Indeed, Order 13 in that case stated that the Intervenors had an opportunity
      to request a hearing before the dismissal, yet the Intervenors failed to avail themselves of the
      opportunity. Notice of the right to a hearing is missing from all SOAH orders granting
      interventions in 59475.​



III. LEGAL ARGUMENT

  A.​ The 180 day period set forth in SB 1076 and in recently amended PURA §37.057 is too short to
      make this hearings process meaningful to intervening landowners. The en masse dismissal of
      Intervenors using procedural hoops like those described above is abhorrent to our system of
      justice. Indeed, the object of the Applicants in these proceedings involves the literal taking of
      thousands of Texans’ most prized possession: their land. These Texans should be afforded every
      legal opportunity to maintain ownership of such an important and valuable asset.
  B.​ The amended §37.057 is not a grant of authority to the Applicants to disregard landowner Due
      Course of Law rights under the Texas Constitution, Tex. Const. art. I, § 19, Due Process rights
      under the U.S. Constitution, U.S. Const. Amend XIV, § 1 or those rights found in the Texas
      Administrative Procedure Act at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051.
  C.​ Section 2001.051 specifically provides:​
      In a contested case, each party is entitled to an opportunity:​
      (1) for hearing after reasonable notice of not less than 10 days; and​
      (2) to respond and to present evidence and argument on each issue involved in the case.
  D.​ The 10 day notice must be adhered to, even within the 180 day time frame set by PURA §37.057
      because Applicant’s CCN cases are contested cases. Certainly “each issue involved in the case”
      includes an unjust dismissal of Intervenor’s entire case for merely failing to file a document.
  E.​ Moreover, when read together, PUC procedural rules 16 TAC 22.124 and 22.161 clearly provide
      for notice and opportunity for hearing before a sanction is issued. En masse dismissal of
      Intervenors, particularly pro se Intervenors who have no particular legal background, without
      providing actual notice of dismissal is especially abhorrent in a condemnation proceeding.
  F.​ The remedy to Applicants of outright dismissal of hundreds of Intervenors, while not providing
      notice or an opportunity for a hearing, is clearly not commensurate with the offense of not
      providing a Statement of Position or Direct Testimony. Procedural rule 16 TAC 22.161 certainly
      provides other alternatives than the death penalty. Consider, for example, 22.161(b)(5):


                                                                                                          4
        disallowing in whole or in part requests for relief by the offending party and excluding evidence
       in support of such requests. This sanction could have been used here, and it would not amount to
       the death penalty for landowners.
   G.​ The fact Applicants did not make a formal motion for dismissal requesting certain sanctions
       effectively reduced their burden to zero. All the Applicants have to do is file a list, and this Court,
       sua sponte has predetermined, in every instance, that the death penalty is appropriate. The
       Applicants in this scenario do not have a burden to show what otherwise might be considered a
       default, which would require a showing of notice, under 16 TAC 183. See also that 16 TAC 181
       requires a hearing unless the facts necessary to support the dismissal are uncontested or are
       established as a matter of law. The instant process is requiring the Applicants only to identify
       who didn’t file one of two documents, and that is the totality of their burden. All appearances
       are that both the 59029 and 59182 cases operated as if a hearing under 16 TAC 161 was not a
       prerequisite or even a due process concern. Considering that these landowners are often pro se
       and are entirely unfamiliar with administrative law, it couldn’t be easier for Applicants to take the
       land they need for their transmission line.
   H.​ Noelke’s Due Course of Law rights under the Texas Constitution, Tex. Const. art. I, § 19, Due
       Process rights under the U.S. Constitution, U.S. Const. Amend XIV, § 1 and those rights found in
       the Texas Administrative Procedure Act at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051 will be violated if
       dismissals result from the list filed by Applicants. The premature en masse termination of party
       status for hundreds of eastern-segment landowners, possibly as many as half of all intervenors,
       fundamentally distorts the routing calculus for the entire integrated project. Applicants’ should
       not be allowed to dismiss these Intervenors.
   I.​ Similarly, Intervenors’ Due Course of Law rights under the Texas Constitution, Tex. Const. art. I,
       § 19, Due Process rights under the U.S. Constitution, U.S. Const. Amend XIV, § 1 and those
       rights found in the Texas Administrative Procedure Act at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051 will be
       violated if dismissals occur as a result of Applicant’s list. A hearings process must be meaningful
       to satisfy Due Court of Law and Due Process, and clearly being dismissed without notice and
       hearing in this manner is not a meaningful process.




III. PRAYER




                                                                                                            5
     A.​ Noelke requests that this Honorable Court disregard Applicants’ LIST OF INTERVENORS
        WHO DID NOT FILE TESTIMONY OR STATEMENT OF POSITION filed in 59475 on May
        15, 2026, Item 4688.
    B.​ He further requests that this Court allow Applicants leave to file a procedurally proper Motion to
        Dismiss all Intervenors it asserts have not filed Testimony or a Statement of Position. Their
        motion should provide notice to the Intervenors of an impending dismissal and a fair, that is 10
        days, notice to cure or a hearing to contest that dismissal.
    C.​ Noelke moves that this Honorable Court requires Applicants to provide actual notice of that
        Motion via First Class U.S. mail, return receipt requested so that notification can be proven, to
        each Intervenor it seeks to dismiss.
    D.​ Noelke also moves that the scheduling order in SOAH Order No. 6 be appropriately amended to
        accommodate these changes and so that the rights of all Intervenors under Due Course of Law
        under the Texas Constitution, Tex. Const. art. I, § 19, Due Process rights under the U.S.
        Constitution, U.S. Const. Amend XIV, § 1 and those rights found in the Texas Administrative
        Procedure Act at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051 are not being subsumed by the 180 day rule in
        PURA §37.057.
    E.​ Noelke also requests other and further relief to which he may be entitled.

Signed May 17, 2026

Respectfully submitted,​
/s/ George Noelke​
George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se landowner​
​
CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a true and correct copy of the foregoing document was served on all parties and counsel of
record on May 17, 2026 with PUC Procedural Rule 22.74 and Orders issued in Docket No. 59182 and
59475.

/s/George Noelke​
George Noelke
